```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 110)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = "/gpfs1/pi/avolaric/files_jrboyd/P3_CosMx_v2")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(data.table); library(ggplot2); library(knitr)})
setDTthreads(1)
ROOT <- "/gpfs1/pi/avolaric/files_jrboyd/P3_CosMx_v2"
## Guarded reads, as in steps 13 and 16: a missing intermediate degrades one block, never
## the render. Everything unavailable is listed in the appendix.
MISSING <- character()
rd <- function(p, ...) {
  f <- file.path(ROOT, p)
  if (!file.exists(f)) { MISSING <<- c(MISSING, p); return(NULL) }
  tryCatch(fread(f, ...), error = function(e) { MISSING <<- c(MISSING, p); NULL })
}
img <- function(p, cap = NULL) {
  f <- file.path(ROOT, p)
  if (!file.exists(f)) { MISSING <<- c(MISSING, p); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  knitr::include_graphics(f, rel_path = FALSE)
}
kb <- function(d, ...) if (!is.null(d) && nrow(d)) knitr::kable(d, ...) else invisible(NULL)
fm <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

# What this step is for

Four names for a cell were in circulation before this step — `inSitu_clusters`,
`pearson_clusters_low/high`, the step-09b audited labels, and the step-16 argmax `celltype` —
they disagreed, and nothing recorded which one a given claim rested on.

Step 19 keeps **two** concepts on purpose, because they answer different questions and fail
in different ways:

- **`celltype_argmax`** — direct per-cell marker evidence. Independent of clustering and of
  QC tier. Silent on most cells.
- **`celltype_cluster`** — guilt by association. A cell with no marker transcripts meeting
  the argmax cutoffs still co-clusters with cells that do, and inherits their name.

Both are needed, and the reason is measurable: **43.4% of the high-confidence set gets no
argmax call at all**. Marker evidence alone leaves nearly half the tissue unnamed. They are
carried as separate columns so no figure can silently mix them; where they disagree, that is
information, not a defect to be reconciled away.

# The substrate

```{r hc-set}
md <- rd("output/16_regions/cells_meta_all.csv.gz",
         select=c("cell_id","samp","is_defect","tier_matched"))
lab <- rd("output/19_celltypes/hc_cells_final.csv.gz", na.strings=c("NA",""))
if (!is.null(md) && !is.null(lab))
  kb(data.table(
    stage = c("all cells", "symmetric QC tier & non-defect", "less the low-information floor"),
    cells = fm(c(nrow(md), md[tier_matched & !is_defect, .N], nrow(lab)))),
    caption = "Building the high-confidence object")
```

The tier is **`tier_matched`** — `qc_spatial_fovpx == "ok" & qcCellsPassed` — deliberately
excluding the staining rule that cost IB1 2,013,225 cells and was never evaluated for RB1.
Any other tier contaminates every IB1-vs-RB1 statement.

**Defect cells are dropped per cell, before clustering, and that is the whole design.**
`09c_script_cluster_consistency.R` showed that pooling launders defect tissue into a lineage
label: merged cluster 1 was 93.6% IB1 cells that IB1's own audit calls `defect_dominated` at
70.1% defect, but pooling diluted that to 42% — under the `DEFECT_MAX` guard — so it escaped
and became "Neutrophil". With no defect cells present there is nothing to dilute. This is why
`CLAUDE.md`'s ban on merged labels does not apply to this object, and only to this object.

A further **60,269 cells (2.93%)** fail a per-cell low-information floor (`nCount >= 50 &
nFeature >= 30`), added after a first build put 159 near-empty cells at UMAP1 ≈ −18 while
99.99% of the object lay between −4.4 and +4.2 — stretching the axis to 4.5× the width the
data needed. They are not lost: they fall to the rescue tier.

## The gate

No cell type was called until the clustering came back clean. The gate asks whether a **large
cluster is resolution-poor**, judged on evidence about cells rather than on cluster
membership, and it **passes at both resolutions**.

```{r gate}
kb(rd("output/19_celltypes/hc_cluster_health_high.csv")[
     , .(cl, cells, pct, pct_IB1, frac_resolved, med_nCount, negrate, top, purity, status = ifelse(junk, "junk", ""))][1:8],
   caption = "Cluster health, resolution 0.8 (first 8 by size)")
```

The gate shipped **broken** on its first run and reported a vacuous PASS: its negprobe term
was a median of per-cell ratios, and `nCount_negprobes` is nonzero in only 21.8% of cells, so
that median is 0 everywhere and `negrate > baseline` read `0 > 0` — false always, inside an
AND. It now uses the pooled ratio and two conditions rather than a four-way AND, which is not
a strict test but an unreachable one.

# The vocabulary

```{r vocab}
if (!is.null(lab)) {
  v <- lab[!is.na(celltype_cluster), .(cells = .N), by = celltype_cluster][order(-cells)]
  v[, `% of high-confidence` := round(100*cells/sum(cells), 2)][, cells := fm(cells)]
  kb(v, caption = "Ten labels, covering 100% of the high-confidence set")
}
```

Six come from **argmax composition** — the modal per-cell call among a cluster's resolved
cells. Two required rules the coarse marker sets could not express, and two are refinements:

- **pDC** and **Hodgkin chemokine niche** were the two largest *unnamed* clusters. Neither has
  a family in `LINEAGE_SETS_COARSE`, so argmax could never call them: pDCs express MZB1 and
  IRF4 and were split evenly between the PC and B sets (purity 0.227 vs 0.225). They are named
  by cluster-level **module rules**, applied only where argmax composition left the cluster
  unnamed, so a module score can never override per-cell evidence that already succeeded.
- **Plasmablast** was separated from Plasma cell after the label proved to occupy two distinct
  positions in the embedding.

**The Hodgkin chemokine niche is a REGION, not a cell type** (`is_niche = TRUE`). Per-cell HRS
calling is a closed avenue on this panel — TNFRSF8 maxes at 6 counts with 78% singletons — so
it is barred from cell-type statements while preserving what is arguably IB1's most important
biology.

Two scoring lessons are built in. **Purity is the wrong yardstick for a minor lineage**: the
object is ~50% B among resolved cells, so NK could not exceed ~0.34 purity and was losing its
label entirely; enrichment over the family baseline is capped at 1/baseline and cannot certify
the *dominant* family, so a cluster now qualifies on **either** route. And the **FDC rule needs
three conditions**: CR2/FCER2 over B_core inflates wherever B signal is thin, and on a first
pass relabelled a 102,783-cell cluster with argmax B purity 0.806 as FDC.

# Validation

```{r heldout}
img("output/19_celltypes/figures/marker_heatmap.png")
```

Panel A is circular by construction — those genes named the labels. **Panel B is the
evidence**: canonical markers no step-19 rule ever looked at. Every one of the ten labels tops
its own held-out set. **Plasmablast ranks second on *both* parent sets** (B 4.68 behind B cell
5.11; plasma 1.52 behind Plasma cell 1.89), which is the signature of a genuine intermediate
and could not have arisen if it were a mislabelled subset of either.

```{r composition}
img("output/19_celltypes/figures/composition_figure.png")
```

Panel C opens each label up. Agreement with argmax runs **66.2%** across the high-confidence
set, and where it is low the reason is legible rather than mysterious.

## Cross-sample marker comparisons need matched cells

```{r bdisc}
kb(rd("output/19_celltypes/b_discrepancy_slopes.csv"),
   caption = "Within-IB1 gradient: slope of B-marker signal on the non-B neighbour fraction")
```

The by-sample heatmap initially showed IB1's B markers far weaker than RB1's. That is **the
label, not the biology**: IB1's B label is 14.8% argmax-confirmed at a median 221 counts,
against RB1's 51.3% at 658. Restricted to confirmed cells IB1's share is *higher* (73.6 vs
68.3); depth-matched it settles at ~10–15% lower, consistently.

**Dilution was the leading hypothesis and it is refuted.** Dilution predicts share falling
while count holds; the observed pattern is the opposite — absolute count falls significantly
(−1.11 [−1.41, −0.77]) while share does not move. The pooled figure is preserved as
`*_v1_POOLED_SUPERSEDED.png` with `README_marker_heatmap_versions.md` beside it.

# The rescue

```{r rescue}
kb(rd("output/19_celltypes/all_cells_celltypes.csv.gz", select=c("cell_id","confidence"))[
     , .(cells = fm(.N)), by = confidence][order(-nchar(cells), cells)],
   caption = "Every cell in the study, by confidence class")
```

Cells outside the high-confidence object are projected into its PCA and take a 25-nearest-
neighbour vote. **Expression space only — never spatial**, because a spatial vote manufactures
exactly the halo artefact step 18 measured.

Two gates were fixed in the script before any numbers were seen. Gate A (held-out
high-confidence cells against their own cluster label) passed at **0.863**. Gate B (rescued
cells against argmax, where argmax resolves) read **0.417** pooled and rejected everything —
but pooled it was averaging two populations that behave nothing alike:

```{r gateb}
kb(data.table(stratum = c("non-defect", "defect"),
              agreement = c(0.677, 0.270),
              `median nCount` = c(475, 623),
              verdict = c("ships", "withheld")),
   caption = "Gate B per stratum (threshold 0.50; the two callers agree at 0.662 inside the high-confidence object)")
```

Applied per stratum it recovers **714,708 cells**, taking labelled coverage to **61.5%**.
Note the depths: defect cells are *deeper* than the non-defect cells that succeed. Their reads
are not scarce, they are wrong — which is also why **imputation is not the remedy**, and why
agreement stays flat at 0.26–0.29 across a 7× depth span.

~370k of the shipped labels are validated by extrapolation from their stratum rather than
directly, since only cells with an argmax call can be checked. The `rescued` tag marks them.

# Where things are

```{r spatial-ct}
img("output/19_celltypes/figures/celltype_spatial.png")
```

```{r spatial-qc}
img("output/19_celltypes/figures/qc_spatial.png")
```

**IB1's over-fixation defect forms a peripheral rim** — fixative penetrating from the outside
in — while **the QC-tier failures form an FOV grid**, a tiling artefact. Different mechanisms,
and the rescue recovers the grid while correctly leaving the rim alone. IB1's maps therefore
stay sparse at the section margins and are well covered in the cores.

Each panel is scaled to its own type, with the ceiling printed in the strip: **colour is not
comparable between panels**, only pattern within one. That was the only way to keep minor
types visible when B reaches 89% of a bin in RB1.

# What this step cannot support

- **A cluster-level plasma-cell claim without conditioning.** The halo test flagged Plasma
  cell at 12.7×, and the flag was wrong: conditioning on the cell's own light chain collapsed
  it to 1.6×. Rising lines in that test are the *expected null* — cell types cluster, so a
  cell with no markers beside a marker-rich neighbour genuinely is more likely to be that type
  with dropout. A high fold now sets `needs_conditioning`, never `halo_suspect`.
- **T-cell subsets from clustering.** Tested three ways and it fails every time; T stays a
  single label and Tfh comes from the per-cell argmax subsets, as step 16 already does.
- **Any label for the 1.65M over-fixation-defect cells.** They are `unresolved` and should
  stay so.
- **Per-cell leakage correction of any kind.** Every candidate score is at chance
  (AUC 0.35–0.61). Leakage is real at the population level and unmeasurable per cell.
- **Cross-sample marker comparisons on pooled label cells.** Use argmax-confirmed cells within
  depth strata.
